appendsTo: pan-stop-study-05.json (r3 pan); this file covers the POWERED holding condition

model.base: study 05 r3 configuration: props, 5420 N m/rad stow stop + 1.5 N m spring, 4050 N m/rad soft stop, -3.5 deg opening-only inhibit
model.drive: 30 A limit, registered controller (65/2.5/15 at 50 Hz), 9 V branch bound, holding stow
model.clutch: pan_stop_06.mjs: Coulomb slip clutch between the reflected rotor (3e-6 or 9e-6 kg m2 x ratio^2) and the pan; gearbox output torque = clutch torque
model.events: extra chassis acceleration at carry start + 2.0 s on both pipe and pan (pan_stop_05 pulse law)
model.supportMonitor: pan_stop_06s.mjs: the solver carry-support test (pan load >= 0.5 M g and both side loads >= 0.03 N) applied over the whole carry, not only its first 1.6 s

frontAbuse.description: 12.34 kN front bumper strike: 180 m/s2 for 20 ms (opening)

rearAbuse.description: 12.34 kN rear strike: 180 m/s2 for 20 ms (closing, into the stow pads)

findings: Powered at 30 A, every event keeps both pipes in the pan, releases them and scores 12/12 with all resets met, including the front bumper strike and 8 g / 50 ms. Peak opening: 3 g 3.9 deg, 5 g 14.3 deg, 8 g 48.1 deg, front strike 51.5 deg, rear strike 3.4 deg (adverse trips govern).

Clutch: with the 3e-6 kg m2 rotor the clutch never slips (peak 12.3 N m in the front strike), so gearbox torque = clutch torque <= 12.3 N m; 16.5 and 18 N m settings give identical results. With a 9e-6 rotor it slips for 4-12 ms in the front strike and 8 g events and caps the gearbox at 16.5 N m.

Support criterion: the solver carry-support test is interrupted by EVERY event (3 g 24-37 ms, 5 g 41-85 ms, 8 g 74-114 ms, front 82-95 ms, rear 67-73 ms); the article hops and re-seats. A perfectly latched pan shows the same hop (3 g 24-25 ms, front 134-136 ms), so no latch, holding current, stiffer stop or stow angle removes it. It is an article-retention (lid/guide) question, not a pan-hold failure. Roll-out custody is kept in all cases.

Voltage: the conservative branch bound (lowest bus paired with peak pan power) falls below 9 V for the 8 g (8.82 V) and front-strike (8.81 V) adverse trips and is 9.14 V at 5 g. The simultaneous bus at the 30 A pan instant is >= 10.14 V, giving a simultaneous branch of >= 9.09 V (front strike; 9.45 V at 8 g); the shortfall is in the conservative pairing, not a simultaneous sag.
Support margin after these events is >= 1.8263 mm (3 g, -2.0 um vs baseline) and >= 1.8286 mm for 5 g and stronger; reset margins fall to 38-40 ms for 8 g and the front strike.

smallestFix.needed: No pan-hold fix is needed for powered custody. The two open items are (1) the article hop under the continuous-support test and (2) the conservative 9 V bound for >= 8 g or bumper strikes.

holdOptionsAssessed.latch: latched-pan control: hop persists (front strike 136 ms); a latch would also add mechanism and does not help the voltage bound beyond removing the recovery current
holdOptionsAssessed.higherHoldingCurrent: raises pan power during the event and worsens the conservative branch bound; custody already kept at 30 A
holdOptionsAssessed.stifferStop: only acts in closing; the events that matter open the pan
holdOptionsAssessed.stowAngle: not evaluated quantitatively; would change every feed/release clock and needs the full 12-case basis again

smallestFix.recommendation: Accept powered holding; decide whether the continuous-support test applies to abuse/peer events (if yes, add an article retainer and retest), and either accept the conservative bound for >= 8 g events or limit pan current during carry recovery (e.g. 20 A carry-phase limit) and re-run.

limits: Peer contact modeled as rigid chassis acceleration pulses; no bumper force history.
Clutch is ideal Coulomb with a fixed set torque; breakaway scatter and stick-slip not modeled.
Branch voltage uses the existing clocked-bus envelope; event current is not added to the chassis drive load beyond the replayed pan current.
